More of our work →

How the loop works

Research → Design → Product → Research

  1. 01Understand
  2. 02Shape
  3. 03Run

What do people actually need?

We watch real people use your product, service, or website, in our Arlington lab or remotely. We recruit the right participants, moderate the sessions, and tell you what we saw, not what we assumed.

In practice

A federal agency learns that most people abandon a benefits form at the same question, and why.

Explore Research →

What should the experience be?

Using Human-Centered Design (HCD), we turn findings into journey maps, service blueprints, and prototypes, then test them again with the same kinds of people. Accessibility and Section 508 compliance are part of the work from the start.

In practice

The form is redesigned around how applicants describe their situation, and tested until they finish it.

Explore Design →

How does it keep working?

Some problems show up across many clients. For those, we build and support software: Chirp, Edjit, CXAlign, and Mediabarn Time. Each one is tested with its users, which sends us back to research.

In practice

A health system tracks every patient experience initiative in CXAlign and sees where the next round of research is needed.

Explore Product →

…and back to Understand.

Every product we run and every design we ship goes back through research. That’s the loop, and it’s why the work gets better over time.

Software that came out of the work.

We kept seeing the same problems across clients, so we built tools for them. Each one runs on the same research and design methods as our client work.

  1. ChirpFor country clubsMembers, events, and RSVPs in one place, so club staff spend less time on spreadsheets and more time with members.→
  2. EdjitFor government contractorsAn eLearning platform for building internal courses and tracking who has completed them.→
  3. CXAlignFor healthcare leadersOne clear view of patient experience work: priorities, initiatives, research, and the teams moving it forward.→
  4. Mediabarn TimeFor professional services teamsTrack time, bill clients, see where team hours go, and measure performance, without enterprise pricing.→
